evidence.note: Reconnaissance reads RFC sections roughly in dependency order (frame header, blocks, literals, FSE, Huffman, sequences), showing implicit awareness of the natural ordering — but this is spec reading, not build milestones.

A single apply_patch (step 22) is the only code write before the first build (step 24) and test (step 26). The whole decoder is written in one push before running anything — matching the level-0 anchor of a monolithic write.

Long uninterrupted edit→make→run debug loop against the same input (audio.wav.zst), patching the monolith over and over. No component is built, isolated, and confirmed done before the next; failures are chased inside one big implementation rather than localized by staged milestones.
Late fixes (checksum, cleanup) are still patches to the single monolith followed by full test.sh runs — no per-component completion criteria ever established.

reasoning: The agent wrote the entire decoder in one patch (step 22) before any build or run, then spent the whole remainder in a monolithic debug loop — the defining pattern of the level-0 anchor. It rises slightly above pure 0 only because its RFC reconnaissance (steps 13-19) followed the format's dependency order, giving a loose implicit ordering. There are no explicit, independently-verifiable milestones (raw → RLE → literals → FSE → Huffman → sequences → dictionaries) with per-stage done-checks, placing it between the 0 and 3 anchors, closest to 2.
